For the supercritical case $p > p_c := 1 + \fracσ{N}$, we prove the small-data global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions in weighted Sobolev spaces $H^{σ/2,m}(\mathbb{R}^N) \times H^{0,m}(\mathbb{R}^N)$ by closing a bootstrap argument. For the subcritical ($1 < p < p_c$) and critical ($p = p_c$) cases, we establish precise lower bounds for the lifespan $T_\varepsilon$ of blow-up solutions via delicate ODE analysis. Together with the corresponding upper estimates, our results fully determine the sharp lifespan estimates for all $β\in [-1, 1)$, confirming that $p_c = 1 + \fracσ{N}$ is indeed the critical exponent for the fractional wave equation with time-dependent damping.
papers.title: Weighted Fractional Commutator Estimate and Application to the Fractional Wave Equations with Time-dependent Damping

papers.abstract: We present new results on polyomino nets that fold into four or five distinct boxes. With the help of AI, we first found examples with areas 532 and 2128, respectively. We analyze these examples and reduce their areas to 178 and 358, respectively. We also generalize the construction of the five-box net and show that infinitely many polyomino nets fold into five distinct boxes.
papers.title: Polyominoes Folding into Four and Five Distinct Boxes

papers.abstract: In this paper we consider cycles of singular algebraic foliations on the real projective plane. Our first result shows that there exists a limit cycle of singular algebraic foliations such that the limit cycle cannot be realized in any affine chart, that is, it fails to appear in any affine plane via the usual dehomogenization. On the other hand, under an appropriate convexity assumption, we verify that a cycle becomes fully visible, lying entirely in some affine chart. We then analyze the accumulation behavior of limit cycles of singular algebraic foliations on the real projective plane. Last we prove that algebraic foliations of degree at most two on the real projective plane have only finitely many limit cycles, and the maximum number of limit cycle is zero, one and at least six for algebraic foliations of degree zero, one and two on the real projective plane, respectively. This result extends Bamon's finiteness theorem for quadratic affine vector fields in [Publ. Math. IHÉS, (64)1986, pp. 111--142].
papers.title: Limit cycles of singular algebraic foliations on the real projective plane

papers.abstract: Counterfactual sketch animation explores how a static sketch evolves under a hypothetical intervention. We present CounterSketch, a physics-grounded framework that transforms natural-language ``What if...?'' queries into physically plausible sketch animations. The framework integrates VLM-guided scene grounding, causal event-chain reasoning, constraint-based trajectory generation, and verification. It models physical transitions to update the scene graph, computes continuous object trajectories, and validates them against physical, geometric, and semantic constraints. The verified trajectories are then projected into object-level motion bounding boxes to guide downstream sketch-video synthesis. Experiments on CounterSketchBench (80 questions) demonstrate that physics-grounded trajectories provide stronger motion guidance than direct VLM predictions.
papers.title: CounterSketch: Physics-Grounded Counterfactual Reasoning for Sketch-to-Video Generation

papers.abstract: We compare linking-form bounds with the smooth and locally flat nonorientable 4-genera of low-crossing knots. For every prime knot with at most 13 crossings whose Witt-level linking-form bound is at least 2, this bound equals both genera. We also exhibit 41 prime knots with 12 or 13 crossings that bound locally flat Möbius bands but no smooth ones, and whose smooth nonorientable 4-genus is 2. Our methods combine linking forms, Heegaard Floer correction terms and definite-lattice obstructions with explicit band constructions. They determine 3,300 of the 3,525 values left unknown in KnotInfo on 2 November 2026; the remaining 225 knots have range $[1,2]$. We obtain new lower bounds of 2 for 2,102 knots with 14 crossings and correct previously reported values for three knots with 11 crossings.
papers.title: Smooth and Topological Nonorientable Four-Genera of Low-Crossing Knots

papers.abstract: Diffusion-based data augmentation has emerged as a powerful strategy for addressing data-scarce image classification. Recent pipelines typically adapt a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model to a limited number of class examples and subsequently sample synthetic images using diverse textual prompts. However, in extreme data-scarce regimes such as long-tailed single-sample settings, this approach suffers from a dual failure mode: the generated samples often lack discriminative foreground details crucial for classifier training, and the adapted class prior can bias the early denoising process, causing output images to exhibit similar patterns despite varying text prompts. To overcome these limitations, we propose a sampling-side framework of two complementary components that simultaneously enhance fine details and diversity. First, Mask-Guided Reference (MGR) Attention updates only foreground value tokens with reference features via zero-shot segmentation, limiting reference influence to the target object and mitigating excessive global feature injection. Second, Repulsive Noise Optimization (RNO) encourages initial noise trajectories to diverge from dominant generative modes of the adapted model, enabling target prompts to express broader contextual variation. Extensive evaluations show consistent improvements, with the largest gains in long-tailed single-sample settings of up to 2.50 and 2.94 points on CUB-LT IF100, and further robustness across few-shot and background-shift evaluations.
papers.title: Improving Diffusion-Based Augmentation for Data-Scarce Image Classification via Mask-Guided Reference Attention and Repulsive Noise Optimization

papers.abstract: Video games provide a practical setting for collecting vision-language-action (VLA) data, whose acquisition in physical environments is costly. Existing datasets, however, remain limited by restricted game coverage, sparse language supervision, or temporal hierarchies that do not necessarily reflect changes in task objectives. We introduce AceAction, a dataset of human gameplay across multiple 3D games for learning skill composition and subgoal transitions. AceAction organizes demonstrations around complete tasks, linking overall instructions, ordered subgoals, and local skill instructions to temporally aligned visual observations and keyboard-and-mouse actions. To construct these annotations, we develop a vision-language model pipeline that identifies subgoals from changes in objectives or interaction targets, anchors navigation goals to visually recognizable waypoints, and composes adjacent subgoals into task instructions. The resulting demonstrations cover navigation, reconnaissance, combat, interaction, and recovery, with explicit stage boundaries that connect task progression to fine-grained control. We assess annotation quality through model-based verification and human inspection. An audit of 500 trajectories yields a 95.8% pass rate across independent reviewer assessments. AceAction provides a data foundation for studying how agents execute, combine, and switch skills to follow complex instructions in dynamic game environments.
papers.title: AceAction-5M: Hierarchical Goals for Generalist Action Learning Across 3D Game Worlds

papers.abstract: Graph databases are often used to manage relationship-rich data, whose graph structure and attributes may be sensitive. In many applications, a database owner or a service provider evaluates queries over a private graph for a client. Because the graph cannot be fully disclosed and independently re-executing the query may be impractical, the client cannot directly verify the returned result. This creates a need for verifiable graph query evaluation that preserves data confidentiality. We present VerfGraph, a zero-knowledge system for verifiable graph query evaluation, which enables a client to verify that the query result was correctly computed over a committed graph data, without revealing private graph records or intermediate query values beyond the public inputs and what is implied by the query result. Building on the expansion-centric model introduced by the state-of-the-art zero-knowledge verifiable graph query evaluation system ZKGraph (ICDE'26), VerfGraph achieves more efficient and expressive zero-knowledge verifiable graph query evaluation by advancing design in two key ways. First, we propose novel operator-proof methods for core expansion and shortest-path operations that reduce costly sorting and comparison checks and eliminate edge canonicalization for bidirectional expansion. Furthermore, we introduce correctness proofs for count and weighted shortest-path operators, broadening the class of graph queries that can be verified. We evaluate VerfGraph using the LDBC Social Network Benchmark. Compared with ZKGraph on complex IC queries, VerfGraph achieves $33.9\times$-$59.7\times$ speedups in proof generation and reduces peak prover memory by factors of $4.5\times$-$6.6\times$, while maintaining millisecond-level verification and producing sub-MB proofs.
papers.title: VerfGraph: Efficient Zero-Knowledge Verifiable Graph Query Evaluation System

papers.abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) has become a widely used parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for large pretrained models. However, standard LoRA typically assigns a fixed rank profile despite layer- and stage-dependent adaptation needs, while recent adaptive-rank variants often rely on heuristic or first-order signals that provide only an indirect link between rank reallocation and local loss behavior. This leaves the rationale behind each rank reallocation insufficiently interpretable. Motivated by this gap, we propose LIRA (Loss-Informed Rank Allocation), a dynamic-rank LoRA method designed to make online rank reallocation more interpretable. LIRA scores each layer by the estimated magnitude of the local loss perturbation associated with its recent LoRA-factor movements under a second-order approximation, making the basis for each rank change interpretable term by term. By periodically applying DELTA (Displacement-Evaluated Loss-Trajectory Allocation), a displacement-based algorithm for LoRA rank reallocation, LIRA produces discrete effective ranks under matched budgets while remaining compatible with standard (A,B) adapters. On RoBERTa-base GLUE under the La-LoRA/LoRA protocol, LIRA outperforms the uniform-LoRA and adaptive-rank baselines reported under this protocol; Trajectory EMA attains performance competitive with Fixed-point Fisher at lower estimation cost.
papers.title: LIRA: A More Interpretable Dynamic Loss-Informed Rank Allocation for Low-Rank Adaptation

papers.abstract: The standard definition of entanglement entropy in quantum field theory requires regularizing the entangling surface and factorizing the Hilbert space, which in turn involves a choice of boundary conditions at the regularized surface. This raises two natural questions which are open at present. The first is under what conditions there is a choice of boundary conditions that leads to a unitary map between the original Hilbert space and the factorized one, which is a necessary condition for a well-defined entanglement entropy. The second concerns the situation where there are multiple such choices, in which case the question is whether they all yield the same entropy, or at least the same terms usually referred to as universal. Focusing on topological theories and using three-dimensional Chern-Simons theory as a concrete illustration, we show under specified assumptions that different such choices affect only the non-universal terms in the entropy, such that the remaining terms are universal in this sense as well, while we explicitly demonstrate that boundary conditions corresponding to non-unitary maps can change these terms. We then explain how a similar argument applies to two-dimensional conformal field theories and discuss a condition for universality in general theories.
papers.title: On the universality of entanglement entropy in quantum field theory

papers.abstract: We focus on gravitational waves (GWs) observable in pulsar timing array and interferometric searches that are produced by the annihilation of cosmic string-wall networks in axion-like particle (ALP) models. We called this process "catastrogenesis." It produces GWs with a characteristic peaked spectrum. These GWs would not be observable if the ALPs were stable. We thus assume that ALPs decay into two photons before Big-Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN). The large ALP-photon coupling required could induce field dissipation and friction on cosmic walls through interactions with the radiation background. We study the conditions under which these effects are negligible and map the parameter regions yielding observable GW signals onto the usual ALP mass-coupling parameter space. We find that, in these regions, ALPs dominate the energy density of the Universe before they decay, leading to a period of intermediate matter domination, which would leave a clear imprint on the GW spectrum.
papers.title: Observable gravitational waves from unstable ALP catastrogenesis

papers.abstract: We report the discovery of the Seyfert galaxy J234728.73+242745.7 as a recurrent intermediate-type CLAGN with extreme optical/UV variability. Optical spectra spanning nearly three decades reveal Type 1.0$\rightarrow$1.5$\rightarrow$1.2 transitions, accompanied by the disappearance and reappearance of broad He II $\lambda4686$ and a broad-line Balmer decrement evolving from 4.5 to 7.2 and then 2.4. Monitoring reveals coordinated variability from X-rays to the MIR. SED decomposition yields a host-corrected g-band high-to-low-state flux ratio of $5.4\pm0.4$, exceeding the Swift/XRT ratio of $2.7\pm0.8$ across the changing-look transition. This discrepancy may arise from reduced dust extinction, as correcting for the low-state continuum reddening ($A_V^{\rm cont}=0.66\pm0.23$ mag) brings the optical/UV ratios close to the X-ray value, although the correction is model-dependent and intrinsically weaker X-ray variability may also contribute. However, X-ray spectra show no compelling evidence for intrinsic gas absorption or its variability ($N_{\rm H}^{\rm intr}\lesssim5\times10^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$). In contrast, EP/WXT monitoring during the recent high state reveals order-of-magnitude X-ray fluctuations on monthly-to-sub-year timescales, exceeding contemporaneous optical variations. Meanwhile, the radio flux density remains stable at $\sim2$ mJy across all ASKAP observations since mid-2020. Together with optical/UV and MIR variability and the broad He II transition, these results favor intrinsic accretion-state changes as the primary driver, while allowing a secondary contribution from variable obscuration. The source displays a loop-like MIR color--magnitude evolution, likely driven by the delayed response of an extended torus. This recurrent CLAGN offers a laboratory for probing the dynamic response of the broad-line region and circumnuclear dust to accretion-state transitions.
papers.title: Extreme Multiwavelength Variability in the Recurrent Intermediate-type Changing-look Seyfert Galaxy SDSS J234728.73+242745.7

papers.abstract: Separating touching nuclei requires local boundary detail, while cell type classification requires broader morphological context. These requirements also vary with the surrounding tissue environment. We propose the Tissue-Conditioned Adaptive Cross-Branch Interaction Network (TCINet), a single-stage model with Task-Specific Feature Adapters (TSFA) and Tissue-Conditioned Task-Aware Cross-Branch Interaction (TC-TACBI). TSFA produces branch-specific features at skip connections, and TC-TACBI controls three asymmetric paths among nucleus-presence (NP), horizontal-vertical (HV), and nucleus-type (NT) branches using predicted tissue probabilities. On PanNuke under standard three-fold cross-validation, TCINet achieves multiclass and binary panoptic quality scores of 0.519 and 0.692, respectively. Zero-shot tests on MoNuSeg yield a detection F1 score of 0.876. On PanNuke fold 0, adding TC-TACBI increases mPQ from 0.505 to 0.525. Code is available at https://github.com/celestial1321/TCINet.
papers.title: TCINet: Tissue-Conditioned Adaptive Cross-Branch Interaction Network for Nuclei Instance Segmentation

papers.abstract: A solid-state drive cannot overwrite data in place, so it cleans full blocks by copying out still-valid data, costing speed and lifetime. Interfaces such as NVMe Flexible Data Placement (FDP) let the host label data by expected lifetime so data dying together is stored together, and published schemes report cutting these copies by 20--75%. Those studies rarely state which blocks the drive chooses to clean. Varying only this choice in simulation, we show it decides how much a label is worth: label value peaks when the drive searches moderately for blocks holding little valid data, falls when it always takes the block with the least, and turns negative when it ignores how much valid data blocks hold. This holds in 47 of 48 synthetic configurations, and one real mail-server trace shows the same shape at about half the magnitude. Priced as spare capacity, a two-class label is worth 65% more spare when each scheme runs at its best setting, but becomes a net loss at 20% label error, typical of learned classifiers. Labels stating which data die together keep most of their value at 16 FDP handles and gain as cleaning improves. Evaluations must report the drive's cleaning policy.
papers.title: The Unreported Variable:Collector Selectivity in Data Placement Evaluation

papers.abstract: Foot ulcers are a leading cause of lower limb amputation, and the highest burden often falls on low and middle income regions where specialists and computing hardware are both scarce. Wound monitoring tools are most useful there when they are accurate yet small enough to run on ordinary devices, but accuracy usually comes from heavy networks. We present LINDA, a compact model that grounds segmentation in an explicit structural prior instead of raw intensity. A Local Self-Similarity (LSS) map, computed directly from the image and stable under local lighting changes, is fused into a ResNet-34 encoder, and a small Liquid Time-Constant module refines the boundary over four iterative steps. With every model trained under one protocol on the FUSeg 2021 dataset, LINDA obtains the best Dice (86.68\%), IoU (79.67\%), and boundary accuracy (HD95 6.37 pixels) in our comparison while using only 25.70M parameters, fewer than the U-Net and transformer baselines. As the LSS map is a fixed function of the input, it exposes the structural cues the model follows in a readable form. Together this makes LINDA an accurate, inspectable, and lightweight option for wound assessment in resource-constrained care.
papers.title: LINDA: Low Resource Foot Ulcer Segmentation using Local Similarity and Iterative Neural Dynamics

papers.abstract: In this article we establish new obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings by combining the values of irreducible characters of the Grothendieck ring with the Galois symmetry of the induced unit object $I(1)$ in the Drinfeld center. As a result, we show that a near-group ring of type $G+m$, where $G$ is an abelian group and both $|G|$ and $m$ are odd, can only categorify if $m=|G|$.
papers.title: Galois-modular obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings

papers.abstract: Power-grid customer service increasingly relies on community social media, where customers describe outages, billing, and equipment faults in informal regional dialect. Such messages exhibit non-standard morphology, semantic drift, and out-of-vocabulary expressions that make manual lexicon construction costly and degrade conventional NLP tools. We propose a weak-supervision framework constructing a regional slang lexicon from curated dialect anchors and power-domain seed terms. Candidates are generated via Pointwise Mutual Information with soft-label bidirectional anchoring, retaining dialect-anchored terms while recording power-domain relevance as separate metadata, and are scored by combining Sentence-BERT semantic similarity with a jieba-based wordhood measure. Uncertainty-aware active learning with rule-based and retrieval-augmented LLM oracles is applied under three query strategies, and the resulting lexicon is evaluated by a higher-capability LLM calibrated against human expert annotations via Cohen's $κ$. On 11,177 real WeChat messages from Yuxi (Yunnan, China), the framework achieves an evaluator-estimated dialect precision of DP~$=$~1.0 with zero false positives. An ablation shows that soft-label layering retains 751\% more candidates than strict power-gating at identical precision, expanding the candidate pool from 41 to 349 terms. Human calibration ($n=46$) yields $κ_{\text{dialect}}=1.0$ and $κ_{\text{power}}=0.85$. The resulting 25--33-term lexicon, 4--5 of which are power-relevant, provides a preliminary resource for dialect-aware power-grid service NLP.
papers.title: Constructing a Regional Slang Lexicon for Electricity Demands via Soft-Label Bidirectional Anchoring and Active Learning

papers.abstract: We present an exact computational proof that the frozen QPLIB_2096 instance has global minimum 7,025,720. The solution and certification approach was explored and refined through ZiYor, a self-evolving AI system. The authors provide the mathematical account and exact validation reported here. The original formulation has 300 binary variables, 6,900 triangle inequalities, and 25 nonconvex quadratic constraints. A coefficient-level reconstruction identifies its variables with the unordered pairs of 25 items. The triangle inequalities encode partitions, while each quadratic constraint becomes a bound on the total weight of edges incident to one partition block. This yields a set-partitioning formulation over all capacity-feasible blocks, with a separate edge-cost graph determining the objective. Exact enumeration examines 245,505 subsets of sizes one through six and finds 14,981 feasible blocks. Every six-element subset is infeasible; nonnegative capacity weights exclude all larger blocks. An integer price vector satisfies the dual inequality for every feasible block and has sum 2,229,456. Subtracting this sum from the total objective edge cost 9,255,176 gives a lower bound of 7,025,720, attained by the supplied six-block partition. Fresh solver-free checks validate the candidate against both frozen model formats and verify the certificate. The result is an instance-specific optimality proof with an exact primal and dual witness; no cross-instance performance conclusion is drawn.
papers.title: Exact Optimality Certification of QPLIB 2096 through Complete Set Partitioning

papers.abstract: Strong coupling between collective excitations provides a route to controlling quantum states of matter, yet its evolution under thermal fluctuations remains poorly understood. In the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3, strong magnon-phonon coupling is established at low temperatures. At the same time, recent terahertz experiments revealed the counterintuitive stabilization of a long-lived metastable magnetic state with an exceedingly long lifetime of 5 msec at the antiferromagnetic transition, not at the base temperature. This was attributed to a strongly coupled spin-lattice scenario, challenging the conventional wisdom that increased magnetic and thermal fluctuations near TN should be detrimental to the coherent control of a metastable phase. Thus it requires an independent examination for correct understanding. Using high-field Raman spectroscopy, we systematically investigate the temperature evolution of magnon-phonon coupling in FePS3. We observe a pronounced avoided crossing between magnon and phonon modes across a wide range of temperatures and find that the coupling strength remains remarkably robust with increasing temperatures. The zero-field magnon-phonon detuning decreases progressively with warming, driving the system toward resonance and thereby enhancing their hybridization near the transition temperature. This anomalous thermal evolution provides the crucial key to understanding the unusual terahertz-driven states recently reported in FePS3. More broadly, our results highlight van der Waals magnets as a promising platform for strong coupling among collective excitations and for controlling magnetic states through light-matter interactions.
papers.title: Thermally enhanced magnon-phonon resonance in van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3

papers.abstract: Recent multimodal agents have shown promising progress in embodied planning and web interaction. However, existing evaluations often rely on simplified tasks with limited combinatorial structure, leaving it unclear whether current agents can robustly integrate perception and reasoning for multi-goal planning under temporal, physical, and multimodal constraints. We introduce DualWorldBench, a unified benchmark for evaluating agent planning under controlled symbolic--temporal and grounded--topological complexity. Built around a shared pickup--delivery interface, DualWorldBench consists of three complementary components: TextWorld, which isolates symbolic planning under varying task compositions and release dynamics; SimWorld, which evaluates grounded path planning under controlled topological variation with text, image, or multimodal inputs; and DualWorld-VQA, a diagnostic suite spanning perception, scene understanding, and planning. Experiments reveal a common gap between local understanding and globally consistent planning. In TextWorld, agents struggle to derive optimal task sequences under interacting temporal constraints; in SimWorld, grounded observations are not reliably converted into feasible action sequences. DualWorld-VQA further confirms that perception and topology understanding do not necessarily translate into constrained planning. Together, these results identify the central challenge as composing symbolic or grounded evidence into globally feasible and efficient multi-goal plans. These findings establish DualWorldBench as a challenging testbed for agents with tighter perception--reasoning--planning integration. All datasets and code are publicly available at our project website https://dualworld.netlify.app/.
papers.title: DualWorldBench: Can Agents Plan Deliveries across Symbolic and Grounded Worlds?

papers.abstract: We analyse 17 years of Fermi-LAT $γ$-ray data toward the middle-aged supernova remnant (SNR) G156.2+05.7, supplemented by radio and CO observations and by published X-ray constraints. An extended $γ$-ray source is detected, well described by a 2D Gaussian template ($R_{68} \sim 0.84^\circ$). This description is preferred over a foreground CO template, whereas the Gaussian and a uniform disc are statistically indistinguishable under the AIC. The spectrum shows evidence for curvature, with a log-parabola preferred over a power law at the $\approx 3.4σ$ level. Multi-wavelength spectral energy distribution (SED) modelling, under the adopted assumptions, suggests a leptonic--hadronic joint scenario consistent with the data, with the Fermi-LAT spectrum favouring a hadronic contribution over a purely leptonic interpretation. However, the proton-dominated alternative remains competitive, so the partition of the GeV emission is model-dependent. In the adopted leptonic--hadronic model, the electron population accounts for the radio synchrotron emission and a leptonic $γ$-ray component, while a steep proton population contributes the remaining hadronic $γ$-rays. Adopting a reference distance $d = 2.7$ kpc, the fitted electron cutoff ($E_{e,\mathrm{cut}}\approx 1.2$ TeV) is compatible with the thermal-dominated X-ray emission, while the proton cutoff is fixed by assumption at $1$ TeV. The northeast and southwest quadrants show enhanced $γ$-ray emission, which may be related to a clumpy or asymmetric surrounding medium. A correspondence with the directions of optical H$α$ filaments is suggested by the quadrant orientation but is not yet established. No significant long-term flux variability is found, consistent with steady emission from an extended source.
papers.title: Fermi-LAT Detection of Extended GeV Emission toward the Middle-aged Supernova Remnant G156.2+05.7

papers.abstract: Disturbances can invalidate the conditions required by a robot's next action even when much of its task program remains useful. A recovery system must therefore choose a response suited to the current state. We present DiMuRe (diagnosis-guided multilevel recovery), a framework for robot-use agents that uses phase-specific evidence and method preconditions to select program reuse or predefined recovery skills, including bounded vision-language-action (VLA) grasping. After the original program exits, a multimodal large language model (MLLM) can generate corrective code from images and execution feedback. Local verification checks the outcome of each recovery attempt. We also introduce LIBERO-Disturb, a benchmark for robustness and recovery under mid-execution disturbances, supporting program-based agents and VLA policies. On 801 scheduled disturbed Encore development cases, Local DiMuRe (program reuse and recovery skills) achieves 77.65% complete-task success, compared with 58.68% for the original program under the same physical-step allowance. Full DiMuRe achieves 81.90% with terminal replanning, an additional step allowance, and early handoff. Local DiMuRe also uses fewer physical steps per scheduled episode than the original program.
papers.title: DiMuRe: Diagnosis-Guided Multilevel Recovery for Robotic Task Execution

papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly shape recommendations across chatbots, e-commerce, and user-generated content (UGC) platforms, creating demand for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) to improve item visibility in generated responses. Existing GEO studies are mainly content-centric, optimizing visibility under general-purpose queries. However, a shared item description usually serves users with different needs and decision goals, resulting in its visibility gains being dependent on the request. To investigate how changing intent affects visibility, we formulate IntentGEO to evaluate shared rewrites across need specificity and decision progression. We revisit existing GEO methods and find that their visibility gains vary across user intents. More critically, learning-based prompt optimization can underperform its handwritten seed on average. Tracing these updates reveals prompt drift from explicit recommendation instructions toward generic promotional tactics. To address this drift, we propose AMO (Anchored Meta-Optimization), which preserves recommendation instructions in a fixed core while learning appended strategies from citation feedback. Across four domains and ten intent states, AMO improves average citation-rank gain by 35% over the strongest prior learning-based baseline and leads on nine states. Ablations show that learned additions improve on the fixed core alone and that AMO outperforms full-prompt optimization initialized from that core. It also achieves the highest gains in an agentic recommendation pipeline and, after separate adaptation, on Doubao, a commercially deployed, closed-source online assistant. These findings highlight user intent as a key dimension of GEO evaluation and support anchored adaptation across recommendation needs and decision stages.
papers.title: IntentGEO: Intent-aware Generative Engine Optimization for Recommendation

papers.abstract: Accurate channel state information (CSI) prediction is pivotal for enhancing system capacity in low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite-terrestrial communications within the sixth-generation vision of global ubiquitous connectivity. However, the extreme mobility of LEO satellites, coupled with significant propagation delays, induces severe channel aging. Existing deep learning (DL) methods often struggle with non-stationary dynamics or generalize poorly across diverse global geographies. To address these challenges, we design the Evo-TFMamba, which is an evolutionary framework integrating time-frequency selective Mamba blocks with meta-learning for generalized CSI prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Evo-TFMamba performs adaptive prediction according to the geographic coverage of LEO satellites. Meanwhile, it significantly enhances the model's generalization ability, particularly when faced with unseen channel environments in LEO satellite communication.
papers.title: Toward Generalized LEO Channel Prediction: A Rapid Adaptation Time-Frequency Mamba Framework

papers.abstract: Sequential forecast intervals are often evaluated by aggregate coverage even when calibration memory is bounded. This can be misleading when economically important states recur after long absences: a recent-only buffer may satisfy its overall coverage target while no longer containing errors from earlier episodes of the returning state. We study this problem in next-day financial range forecasting, holding the forecasting model, conformity score, adaptive update, and memory budget constant while varying the historical residual information available at each query. Recent-only first-in, first-out (FIFO) calibration is near nominal in aggregate but undercovers substantially during high-volatility states in both an exchange-traded fund development panel and a fixed stock panel. An unbounded state-history reference yields a lower observed stress-period interval score; Rare replay yields lower high-VIX interval scores than the matched Recent-n and Hybrid-n controls in both panels, and the state-structured versus recent-only contrast is largest near stress re-entry. Bounded calibration memory is therefore part of the forecasting information design, and aggregate calibration alone can conceal state-specific reliability failures.
papers.title: Aggregate Calibration Can Mask Stress-State Undercoverage: Bounded-Memory Forecast Intervals under Recurrent Financial Stress

papers.abstract: Under expert parallelism, mixture-of-experts (MoE) layers pay all-to-all token dispatch, grouped GEMMs, and a combine step in every layer. In decode each rank holds only 1-256 tokens: dispatch latency and weight traffic dominate while tensor-core utilization is inherently low. In fused operators such as DeepGEMM's Mega MoE, dispatch and computation overlap only by sharing every SM: dispatch warps compete with TMA/MMA and epilogue warps for registers, shared memory, and issue slots; every phase shares one CTA resource budget, synchronization spans the whole SM array, and every replay ends with a workspace-clean pass and a cross-rank barrier. We present GC-MoE, an open-source FP8/FP4 MoE inference operator for NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell GPUs that uses CUDA Green Contexts to split the device into a small communication partition and a large compute partition. Each role gets its own kernel, resource budget, and synchronization domain, so dispatch and GEMM tune independently. A three-node CUDA Graph (four on Hopper with fused shared experts) launches the dispatch and grouped-GEMM kernels as concurrent roots; a token-ring handshake starts computation on the first filled ring blocks, and double-buffered receive counters remove the trailing cross-rank barrier between replays. The compute partition runs operand-swapped tcgen05 block-scaled MMA on Blackwell and register-A WGMMA with in-register FP4 decoding on Hopper, with fused SwiGLU, requantization, and optional shared experts. On 8 H20 GPUs GC-MoE accelerates DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode by 1.188x on average on both the routed and shared-expert suites (peaks 1.296x and 1.353x); on 8 B300 GPUs it accelerates GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash by 1.106x (1.123x with fused shared experts, peak 1.209x), beating Mega MoE at all 54 measured points at matched accuracy. GC-MoE reserves only 20 of 148 SMs on B300 for dispatch.
papers.title: GC-MoE: Overlapping Expert-Parallel Token Dispatch with FP8/FP4 Grouped GEMM via CUDA Green Contexts

papers.abstract: Streaming 3D reconstruction must maintain geometric quality over long inputs within a fixed GPU budget. A pretrained recurrent model provides bounded state, but freezing its backbone also fixes its learned state-observation interactions. We introduce Mamba3R, a jointly designed state-memory adapter that provides a trainable adaptation path without updating the backbone or task heads. A selective state-space mixer jointly transforms native state features and a fixed-capacity auxiliary memory, explicit read and write paths carry information across frames, and a decomposed feedback path regulates what the added memory feeds back. Only 1.28 million adapter parameters are trained. Under a shared periodic-reset protocol, it lowers trajectory error and improves accumulated surface and depth accuracy over recurrent baselines on public indoor and outdoor datasets and robot-recorded traversals, gaining up to 40 percent on one metric. Matched comparisons support both the choice of the mixing operator and the utility of carrying the auxiliary memory across frames. Allocated memory remains unchanged and throughput moves by at most 1.4 percent from one to two thousand frames. Replaying its recorded traversals offline, the platform's RTX 4060 averages 11.7 frames per second within 5.1 GiB with the same checkpoint, a mean throughput covering the 10 Hz sensor rate.
papers.title: Mamba3R: Fixed-Capacity Selective State Memory for Long-Sequence 3D Reconstruction

papers.abstract: A three-region junction in a free real relativistic scalar vacuum in $2+1$ dimensions yields a strictly negative logarithmic contribution to genuine tripartite Rényi multi-entropy for every integer $n\geq3$ and all nondegenerate sector angles. The replica subtraction exactly removes loop classes associated with a single interface. Surviving loops have positive, scale-independent weight, yielding a logarithm whose sign is fixed by the negative Rényi prefactor. The selector is empty at $n=2$. The flat-sheet Friedrichs prescription fixes the scalar operator at the nonmanifold replica apex. It yields a convergent angular spectral formula for the coefficient.
papers.title: Negative Junction Logarithms in Scalar Multipartite Entanglement

papers.abstract: Semi-supervised cardiac image segmentation aims to exploit abundant unlabeled images together with limited annotations, but the reliability of pseudo-label supervision is highly uneven across spatial regions. In a dual-network setting, interior regions are usually more stable, whereas boundary regions, low-confidence areas, and disagreements between networks can introduce noisy supervision. However, existing methods typically impose uniform supervision on all unlabeled pixels, overlooking reliability differences and limiting discriminative learning in challenging areas. To address this issue, we propose R2CL (Reliability-Role Collaborative Learning), a framework for semi-supervised cardiac image segmentation. R2CL models confidence relationships between two networks to assign roles to unlabeled regions: mutually uncertain regions are used for entropy regularization, confidence-discrepant regions for directional knowledge transfer, and mutually confident regions as reliable supervision anchors. Reliability-Role Mixed Cross Learning (RR-MCL) implements these roles through region-mixed training, directional cross-network supervision, and entropy regularization over mutually uncertain regions. Reliability-Transition Prototype Contrastive Learning (RT-PCL) constructs query features from foreground-adjacent reliability-transition regions and learns network-specific class prototypes from mutually confident regions, improving feature discrimination around ambiguous boundaries. High-confidence Context Refinement (HCR) exploits reliable interior pixels and trusted dense blocks within mutually confident regions to complement stable contextual supervision. R2CL achieves stable improvements in region-overlap and boundary-related metrics across multiple datasets, with more evident advantages on the foreground-sparse MVAA-CT dataset.
papers.title: Reliability-Role Collaborative Learning for Semi-Supervised Cardiac Image Segmentation

papers.abstract: Repeated decisions over a shared document create two distinct opportunities: reusing document computation and adapting how question representations score candidate answers. We present Q64, a candidate-scoring system that preserves a frozen 64-layer Qwen3.8-27B text backbone, reuses its hybrid prefix state and intermediate document representations, and jointly trains a residual adapter with a four-layer decoder and candidate-conditioned readout. We used ZiYor, a self-evolving AI system, to explore and refine the Q64 design. We specified the scoring method, implemented the system, and evaluated its accuracy and latency. The final adaptation stage updates 88.66 million parameters using 8,192 selected training views. On a fixed 5,112-item evaluation combining ARC-Challenge, ANLI-R3, and stratified subsets of MMLU-Pro and CMMLU, joint adaptation improves four-benchmark macro accuracy from 66.46% to 74.32%. It remains below the native 27B baseline at 75.68% and AnyJev Qwen3-32B L0 at 76.68%. On a separate synthetic workload with 4,096 document tokens and 50 questions, median cold-request latency is 2.237 seconds, compared with 5.383 seconds for the native baseline and 56.872 seconds for the measured batched AnyJev configuration. Short single-question requests do not share this advantage. The evidence supports an accuracy-latency tradeoff in the evaluated systems, rather than a backbone reduction or an isolated component advantage. Public benchmarks informed earlier development, and real-document multi-question validation remains open.
papers.title: Shared Context Candidate Scoring with Jointly Adapted Readout Networks

papers.abstract: Predicting stock returns requires modeling persistent company relations and time-varying market signals. Graph Neural Network (GNN) approaches combine static priors with dynamic relational graphs, but treat every extracted edge as a trustworthy binary fact, ignoring heterogeneous reliability across relational sources. We propose LENS (LLM-Extracted priors and News-driven Semantics), a static--dynamic graph framework for stock return prediction and ranking that models relational reliability as a first-class signal across the pipeline. On the static side, we extract a multi-relational company graph from a Large Language Model and aggregate it over multiple runs with confidence weighting to downweight low-consistency edges. On the dynamic side, we build a news-driven semantic graph with exponential-decay temporal aggregation to capture changing market context under uneven coverage. A context-dependent gated fusion module rebalances the two graphs at the per-stock, per-day level. On S&P 500, LENS improves AR@5 by 16.4% and SR@5 by 22.6% over the strongest baseline, and on NASDAQ 100 it achieves comparable improvements (15.5% and 20.9% respectively). Ablations isolate each component's contribution, and a human-validation study of sampled relations supports that the aggregation is grounded, providing evidence that reliability-aware LLM relations and news-based semantic graphs carry complementary information for graph-based financial prediction.
papers.title: LENS: Reliability-Aware Stock Prediction via LLM-Extracted Priors and News-Driven Semantic Graphs

papers.abstract: Self-attention has become the standard for modern sequence modeling, enabling Transformers to model long-range dependencies across a wide range of modalities. Despite these advances, its quadratic cost with respect to sequence length remains a significant computational bottleneck. Recent work addresses this limitation by introducing linear variants of self-attention, namely with kernel approximations of the softmax operator. However, their first-order aggregation restricts expressivity and struggles to capture higher-order structure. We propose Linear Stochastic Attention (LiSA), a linear attention plug-in module that enables higher-order token interactions via a stochastic diffusion process based on truncated random walks. LiSA incorporates adaptive locality, favoring semantically similar neighbors to preserve fine-grained structures, while maintaining stable and efficient training. We conduct extensive experiments on classification, semantic segmentation, and object detection tasks and show improved results over state-of-the-art methods.
papers.title: LiSA: Linear Stochastic Attention for Long-Range Visual Modeling

papers.abstract: Tokenization is a fundamental component of modern language models: before a model sees data, its tokenizer has already determined how the data appears. We identify and challenge three myths in the tokenization research literature. Myth #1: Bits-Per-Byte (BPB) is agnostic to the tokenizer and/or the vocabulary size: BPB is tokens per byte times bits per token, and the two factors do not cancel; using untrained models, we show that BPB prefers some tokenizers over others: the model has learned nothing, but the tokenizer--model pair has. Myth #2: lower BPB means a better model: On untrained models, BPB strongly prefers some vocabulary sizes, even though accuracy remains at chance, and on real models trained on the same data, BPB correlates weakly with downstream performance. Myth #3: different "tokenizer-agnostic" metrics yield consistent results: The "unigram-normalized loss" is not tokenizer-agnostic; its reported correlation of 0.989 with BPB comes from a confounder and falls to 0.057 once fixed; from the same data the two metrics select different vocabularies at each model size. We present a tokenizer trilemma: no metric can score only the true distribution best, give the same predictions the same score, and tie all untrained models, so choosing a metric is choosing a research question. We conclude with a caution for reading the tokenization literature and a conjecture for future work.
papers.title: Tokenizer Myths and Where To Find Them

papers.abstract: We study the superfluid phases of a two-dimensional degenerate Fermi gas in an optical lattice subject to a $d_{xy}$-wave altermagnetic term that couples to the in-plane spin component. The single-particle Hamiltonian generates anisotropic Fermi surfaces for the two pseudo-spin species while maintaining zero net polarization. Using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes approach, we show that this anisotropy favors Cooper pairing at a finite center-of-mass momentum, producing a competition between Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) and Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) pairing and leading to FFLO superfluids. We further examine the effect of a Zeeman-induced spin polarization and find that triplet and singlet pairing channels coexist and compete, resulting in a momentum-selective pairing pattern. Remarkably, this triplet pairing emerges exclusively in the FFLO phase and is entirely absent in the BCS phase. The model is readily realizable in ultracold atoms with current experimental techniques, providing a feasible route for quantum emulation and for studying unconventional superfluid phases.
papers.title: Altermagnetism-induced Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov superfluids and momentum-selective pairing channels in optical lattices

papers.abstract: The AI labs' vision is based on extraction (of data, wealth, and political power). Mathematicians must oppose it, moving past personal reflections and towards reforming mathematics' social contract.
papers.title: It is time for a New Deal for mathematics

papers.abstract: Interval-censored multistate data arise when subjects are observed at irregular visit times, leaving transition times and intermediate states unobserved. Likelihood-based inference for continuous-time Markov models often requires computationally intensive matrix exponential evaluations. We propose a deterministic uniformization expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm for parameter estimation and latent trajectory inference. By representing the continuous-time process through an embedded Markov chain indexed by latent Poisson event counts, the method enables deterministic E-step calculations without repeated matrix exponential evaluations. The M-step reduces to transition-specific Poisson regressions with exposure offsets, accommodating covariate-dependent transition intensities. We establish uniform truncation error bounds and show that the procedure is an asymptotically monotone generalized EM algorithm. Under standard regularity conditions, the estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal. Simulations demonstrate accurate estimation and computational advantages over direct likelihood optimization, particularly for complex transition structures. We also develop an exact dynamic programming method to calculate posterior probabilities of candidate latent pathways and identify the most probable pathway between observations. Posterior expected transition counts and state occupancy times provide additional subject-specific summaries, while expected-count ratios offer a computational shortcut for classification in simple mutually exclusive pathway structures. The framework supports both population-level inference and individualized characterization of disease progression.
papers.title: Deterministic Uniformization for Estimation and Latent Trajectory Inference in Interval-Censored Multistate Triansition Models

papers.abstract: Set separation by continuous linear functionals is fundamental in functional analysis and convex optimization and underlies binary classification in machine learning. Support vector machines provide maximum-margin affine separators for linearly separable data, while kernel methods represent nonlinear decision rules through linear separation in a reproducing-kernel Hilbert space. We study when two classes, not necessarily convex or linearly separable in the input space, can be separated with positive margin by finite ReLU networks and by random ReLU features. At the deterministic level, we prove that positive-margin separation by a finite ReLU network is equivalent to the existence of finite closed convex covers whose opposite-label members have positive pairwise distances, and exactly two hidden layers suffice. For random separation, suppose each class is represented as a finite union of nonempty closed convex cells, possibly unbounded. If every opposite-label cell pair has positive distance and its closed difference cone is pointed, then two independent random ReLU layers yield a common positive-margin affine separator with high probability. The first layer separates the feature image of each negative cell from the feature image of the positive class by a hyperplane through the origin. It also controls all cross-class distances uniformly. The second layer combines cellwise scores through Chebyshev polynomials and realizes the resulting polynomial using Gaussian Hermite features, followed by a uniform finite-width approximation. With the remaining geometric, bias, and confidence parameters fixed, each sufficient width is quadratic in the largest Gaussian width of a spherical difference-cone section, hence at most linear in its span dimension. An example shows that this squared Gaussian-width dependence is sharp for both layers.
papers.title: Two-Layer Random ReLU Networks Can Separate Disjoint Classes

papers.abstract: We establish an analogue of the Hilbert irreducibility theorem for all K3 surfaces over number fields that admit an automorphism of positive entropy. Our method draws ingredients from both algebraic geometry and complex dynamics.
papers.title: Rational points on loxodromic K3 surfaces and complex dynamics

papers.abstract: Lunar seismic records are characterized by long-lasting spindle-shaped coda, which has long been considered to be caused by strong velocity contrasts in a continuous-medium lunar crust; however, simulated waveforms could not well match the observation even with unrealistically strong velocity contrasts, demonstrating its mechanism still unsolved. Here we propose a novel model of coda wave generation with random fractures in the lunar crust, where vacuum fractures prevent seismic wave propagation as insulating boundaries, causing strong persistent reverberation in terms of total reflection among fractures. Our model can easily reproduce the typical characteristics of observed Apollo data even using a limited number of simplified fractures in homogeneous matrix, with envelope correlations over 0.9, much higher than previous studies. Numerical simulations suggest that fractures in the uppermost ~1 km of the crust may dominate lunar seismic scattering. This model enables us to investigate the shallow lunar fracture system using seismic data and to suppress seismic coda for detecting critical phases reflected from deep interiors.
papers.title: Shallow lunar fractures dominate the long-lasting seismic coda

papers.abstract: Satellite dwarf galaxies are reshaped by the tidal field of their host, a process that may account for part of the structural diversity of the observed dwarf population. We study how the stellar component of a satellite responds to tidal stripping using a suite of 480 controlled $N$-body simulations of satellite galaxies consisting of both dark matter (DM) and stars orbiting a Milky-Way-mass host. The simulated dwarfs span a broad range of DM halo structural and stellar-distribution parameters, including halo concentration, inner density slope, stellar-to-halo mass ratio, compactness of the stellar distribution with respect to the halo, as well as the Sérsic index of the stellar profiles. We present a comprehensive library of tidal tracks, namely, the evolution of the stellar mass, half-mass radius, mean surface density, and line-of-sight velocity dispersion, as functions of the bound mass fraction of the hosting DM subhalo, and provide simple and accurate fitting functions. We also identify the dependence of tidal tracks on key factors in the initial structural conditions. Notably, stellar compactness determines the duration over which the stellar mass remains relatively intact while the surrounding DM is being stripped. The Sérsic index and inner DM slope, in turn, govern the late-stage stellar mass-loss slope and the contraction or expansion of the remnant. Our simulations and empirical models provide a framework for modelling the stellar evolution of satellites across a broad range of progenitor structures, useful for semi-analytical models of satellite galaxy evolution.
papers.title: Tidal Evolution of Satellite Dwarf Galaxies. I. Tidal Tracks of Stellar Mass and Structure

papers.abstract: Motivated by the expressive power of neural ordinary differential equations in flow-based generative modeling, we study the approximation of probability measures by pushforwards generated by parameterized families of Lipschitz vector fields. For Wasserstein distances, we establish a quantitative relationship between finite-sample point interpolation and distributional approximation, and derive universality criteria based on $L^p$-approximation of transport maps. In particular, affine-invariant families containing a non-affine vector field are universal from compactly supported absolutely continuous base measures. For total variation, we show that coordinate-wise dynamics are insufficient in dimensions $d\geq 2$ and establish sufficient conditions based on one-dimensional Sobolev approximation and shear-type mixing. We further examine the role of point interpolation, establishing when different regimes relate to one another and when approximate interpolation can be made exact.
papers.title: Point interpolation and distributional universality in flow-based generative models

papers.abstract: Is AI taking over software engineering research? By 2025, AI appeared in more than half of the research-track papers at ICSE, FSE, and ASE. Yet ubiquity alone cannot show whether AI expanded the publication portfolio, displaced other work, or redirected the intellectual agenda. We investigate this shift through a census of 4,790 research papers (three SE conferences; 2018--2026) and free-form responses from 244 SE researchers discussing the future of the SE research community (ICSE 2026 FoSE survey). We found that while AI is taking over, it is not simply replacing non-AI research; it is unevenly reorganizing SE research around its capabilities. AI accounted for 93.1% of publication growth, but expansion in some venues and problem areas concealed contraction in others. The LLM wave also changed the field's tools more than its problem boundaries: 92.6% of LLM-wave AI papers revisit established SE problems, while most new problems arise from the introduction of LLMs in the SE process themselves. Engagement with AI remains predominantly downstream: 95.7% of AI papers apply AI or evaluate and support its use, while only 4.3% interrogate the paradigm or develop alternatives. The FoSE survey reveals a similar imbalance between recognition and response. AI-driven change was the second-most frequent concern about the field's future 20.2%, yet only 7.0% of responses mentioned AI when researchers were asked to identify one change the community should make. Together, our findings reveal a field reorganizing an inherited agenda around AI faster than it is questioning that reorganization. We discuss how SE can respond by building cumulatively across technological waves, strengthening evaluation and assurance, developing SE-native foundations, and studying software engineering in an AI-transformed world.
papers.title: Are We Just Applying LLMs? What SE Research Studies, Underexplores, and Could Do Next in the LLM Era

papers.abstract: We study the optimal design of investment subsidies across heterogeneous monopolistic markets subject to a common expected discounted budget. Each producer faces a regular one-dimensional demand diffusion and chooses irreversible capacity expansion through a singular stochastic control problem. The regulator values weighted consumer surplus, producer profits, and an additional benefit from installed capacity, while accounting for the excess cost of raising public funds. We characterize producers' optimal investment responses through free boundaries and reformulate the regulator's stochastic optimization problem as a deterministic optimization over investment boundaries. An integral representation then recovers the optimal subsidy schedules that implement the resulting capacity policies. Under mild conditions on the diffusions, we establish existence of optimal schedules and uniqueness of the induced investment policies. Finally, we characterize the subsidy schedule and provide numerical illustrations.
papers.title: Optimal Subsidy Design for Productive Investment across Markets

papers.abstract: Humanoid locomotion requires deciding where to step and how to distribute contact forces. However, a disturbance can invalidate the nominal plan, requiring coordinated revision under constraints that switch with every footfall. To solve this online, the proposed approach employs the single-rigid-body model, which retains attitude dynamics and the full contact wrench. An iterative linear-quadratic-regulator MPC (iLQR-MPC) then jointly optimizes contact forces and footstep locations in a single receding-horizon problem, without a separate step planner. Specifically, contact and motion constraints are incorporated into the backward pass through augmented-Lagrangian and relaxed-barrier penalties. A whole-body controller subsequently maps the plan to joint torques at 500 Hz while preserving contact feasibility. The model-based formulation makes disturbance responses interpretable through explicit costs and constraints, and requires no platform-specific policy training. In MuJoCo simulations, the iLQR-MPC replans at 100 Hz (mean solve time 8.9 ms); the Unitree G1 sustains steady-state walking and recovers from impulsive 245 N forward and 175 N lateral pushes.
papers.title: Online iLQR-MPC with Whole-Body Control for Robust Humanoid Locomotion

papers.abstract: Conventional recommender systems operate within platform-specific catalogs, limiting access to potentially valuable resources across platforms. We propose user-centered agentic recommendation, a paradigm in which user agents compare recommendations from competing platform agents, and formalize their interaction as a repeated game. Platforms strategically modify descriptions without changing intrinsic item value, while each user agent assesses platform credibility using feedback from consumed items only. Our analysis shows that expanded resource access need not improve user welfare: strategic misrepresentation and limited verification can offset the benefits of platform competition. We quantify when platform credibility assessment allows users to benefit from broader access despite strategic exaggeration. Our analysis identifies resource and reporting conditions that guarantee higher average welfare than the original platform with an interaction budget linear in platform count. Experiments on synthetic and Amazon-grounded markets show that credibility assessment can improve finite-horizon utility, while its benefits depend on market size and mechanism parameters.
papers.title: Toward User-Centered Agentic Recommendation: When Does Platform Competition Benefit Users?

papers.abstract: Many processes in chemistry and physics, such as autoionization, photoionization, or electron-impact collisions, involve unbound electrons. Despite their importance, theoretical methods for modeling continuum electrons remain significantly less developed than those for purely bound electronic states. Here we present a novel approach for treating continuum electrons within Gaussian-based quantum chemistry. The method represents continuum orbital in a discrete basis of standard Gaussian-type orbitals (GTOs), where the continuum wave function is obtained by solving the Lippmann-Schwinger equation with proper boundary conditions using an analytical representation of the Green's function in an auxiliary GTO basis set. The resulting continuum orbital is multicentered and multichannel, providing a rigorous description of scattering states. As an initial application of the new methodology, we compute Auger decay rates for several atomic and molecular systems, including Ne, H$_2$O, CO$_2$, and Ar. We demonstrate a consistent improvement of the results with increasing the quality of the continuum representation. We show also that higher-order electron-correlation effects in the bound domain are essential for an accurate treatment of satellite transitions. The present formalism therefore provides a systematically improvable Gaussian-based framework for continuum-electron problems that is fully compatible with standard quantum chemistry methods.
papers.title: Accurate representation of the continuum orbital in a Gaussian basis set: application to Auger decay rates

papers.abstract: We prove local existence and uniqueness, propagation of Sobolev regularity, and continuation criteria results for the characteristic initial value problem for the 3D compressible Euler equations. This is the Cauchy problem with initial data given on a pair of transversally intersecting (acoustically) null hypersurfaces. The region of existence in our main theorem is a future-neighborhood of the union of the data null hypersurfaces, where the size of the neighborhood depends on various norms of the data as well as the structure of the data null hypersurfaces. We allow for any equation of state with positive sound speed, and we do not make any symmetry, irrotationality, or isentropicity assumptions. Our analysis relies on the geometric formulation of the flow derived in [Speck19], which decomposes the equations into a "wave-part" coupled to a "transport-div-curl" part. Compared to Rendall's celebrated solution of the characteristic initial value problem for wave equations [Rendall90], substantial new ideas are needed to handle the fact that the compressible Euler equations are more complicated than pure wave equations.
papers.title: The Characteristic Initial Value Problem for the 3D Compressible Euler Equations

papers.abstract: Deep-learning-based mass detectors usually downsample mammograms, trading fine image detail for lower computational cost. However, published studies cannot reveal how much accuracy this trade-off sacrifices, since they also differ in architecture, preprocessing, and evaluation protocol. In this work, we isolated the effect of input resolution in a controlled study on the VinDr-Mammo dataset, training 18 detectors at six input resolutions ranging from 512 x 416 to 1600 x 1280 pixels, for 108 model-resolution combinations. Whole mammograms were resized without cropping or tiling. For each model, preprocessing, model initialization, augmentation, and evaluation procedures were kept fixed across resolutions. Detection accuracy was evaluated by mAP50 on the 219 mass-positive images of the official test split, and 57 combinations with test mAP50 of at least 0.60 were analyzed. From the lowest to the highest resolution, median mAP50 rose from 0.626 to 0.660 and the best mAP50 from 0.670 to 0.709. The best result, achieved by DINO with a ConvNeXt-S backbone, is the highest mAP50 reported to date on mass-positive VinDr-Mammo images. Gains were concentrated in small masses: for the smallest third of lesions, median mAP50 rose by 0.074 (from 0.367 to 0.441), compared with 0.007 and 0.032 for medium and large masses. Median training time increased from 0.45 to 1.40 h, and median inference time from 23.6 to 113.7 ms per image. Therefore, higher input resolution mainly benefits the small masses that are hardest to detect, at a computational cost that remains practical.
papers.title: Impact of Input Resolution in Mammographic Mass Detection: A Controlled Multi-Architecture Study

papers.abstract: How much label noise has a network memorized, and when? We study a multilayer perceptron and what statistical complexity adds to a description of its predictions. Standard identities decompose predictive information into signal, memorization, and heterogeneity. The memorization term vanishes in the population under the stated noise-independence condition. A Fano-type bound relates it to training accuracies, but the memorized fraction M provides no upper bound. Across 89 MNIST runs with ten pre-specified hypotheses (five supported, four unsupported, one not testable), normalized memorization information rose with M on training samples, remained near zero on held-out samples with fresh noisy labels, and was close to its Fano bound. Unlike raw M, it has a zero population null under the independence condition and chance correction largely removed this difference. When every label was replaced by an incorrect class, test accuracy fell to 0.5%, yet predictions retained information about the true class. Mean statistical complexity peaked before memorization at corruption rates up to 40%. At higher rates, its peak fell within the memorization phase, near the epoch when mean training confidence reached 0.6 and the two could not be separated. As a stopping rule, it matched established rules only at low noise and detected corrupted samples less well than simple label-free scores. An exploratory extension of 280 runs covering Fashion-MNIST, pair-flip noise, and four training variants yielded similar results under uniform noise, but not pair-flip noise, where complexity peaked within two epochs. Conclusions are limited to this architecture, two small datasets, and synthetic noise.
papers.title: An Information Budget for Label-Noise Memorization, and What Statistical Complexity Tracks: A Study with Multilayer Perceptrons

papers.abstract: We study deep variational circuits for a periodic Heisenberg chain under local gate depolarization, at depths where noiseless training is coherently exact. Full-width initializations reach low coherent error faster than circuits with confined transverse generators, but incur a larger noise shift and need an order of magnitude more updates for noisy convergence. In many-body-localization-inspired initialization, bounding the initial transverse generator amplitudes keeps the operator support localized and suffices for low-fragility optimization, so longitudinal disorder and Floquet layer repetition are unnecessary. The fault-erasure fraction, the mean fraction of coherent energy removed per fault, sets the effective visibility through a parameter-free exponential model. Full-width circuits start with delocalized operator support, and once coherent energy builds up, each fault erases nearly all of it. Initially, their noise-induced gradient almost uniformly attenuates the coherent gradient, so coherent descent proceeds at the noiseless rate. They then stall on a high-noise force-balance plateau, where finite coherent and noise-induced gradients cancel to first order. At late times all initializations reach the same fault-erasure fraction and noisy-error band, but operator support contracts more slowly, at a rate set by the plateau residence time.
papers.title: Initialization-controlled fault sensitivity and force-balance plateaus in noisy variational quantum optimization

papers.abstract: The effects of ${}^{12}\mathrm{C}+{}^{12}\mathrm{C}$ fusion and ${}^{12}\mathrm{C}(α,γ){}^{16}\mathrm{O}$ capture on stellar heating, composition, and black-hole masses are examined. Rates from a published Bayesian analysis of carbon fusion are used in calculations with MESA. In an accreting carbon--oxygen white dwarf, the Bayesian rates move the point at which nuclear heating equals combined neutrino and surface photon losses to slightly larger stellar masses and higher central temperatures and densities. At an accretion rate of $10^{-7}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, the Bayesian median gives a central temperature approximately $2.57\%$ higher and a central density $18.9\%$ higher than the calculation using the standard CF88 rate. A separate calculation follows carbon burning in an initially $20\,M_\odot$, $Z=0.0142$ star. Relative to the CF88 rate with MESA's standard division between proton and alpha channels, the Bayesian-median rate with the proton-to-alpha ratio of Yang et al. increases the neon-20 mass remaining at central carbon depletion by $10.8\%$ and decreases the sodium-23 mass by $28.7\%$. For helium capture on carbon, the nuclear constraint $S_{\rm tot}(300\,\mathrm{keV})=118\pm17\,\mathrm{keV\,b}$ is applied to the published $Z=10^{-5}$ stellar models of Farag et al. Linear interpolation gives a maximum black-hole mass below the pair-instability gap of approximately $61.5$--$77.4\,M_\odot$ within the assumptions of those models. New MESA calculations at $Z=0.00142$ give smaller bound masses before collapse. Differences in the stellar assumptions prevent attributing the difference between the two curves to metallicity alone.
papers.title: Carbon-Reaction Constraints on Stellar Evolution: White-Dwarf Heating, Carbon-Burning Products, and Black-Hole Masses

papers.abstract: Frontier LLM agents can turn known vulnerabilities into working exploits, but are costly and often access-restricted due to their potential for malicious use. Open-weight models offer a more accessible alternative, but struggle to maintain progress across long exploitation chains. They also often fail to apply relevant security knowledge at the appropriate stage and in the right context to identify and evaluate promising attack directions. To address these limitations, we propose DoGNAVY-Exploit, a multi-agent harness built around two complementary designs: stage-aware decomposition with progressive expert knowledge disclosure, and hierarchical orchestration with parallel exploration. Specifically, DoGNAVY-Exploit uses configurable milestones to recast long-horizon exploitation as short, verifiable capability transitions and provides only the knowledge relevant to each stage. Within each milestone, a hierarchical architecture separates strategic planning from parallel execution: a planner proposes diverse attack routes, executors test them concurrently, and a controller accepts progress only when supported by runtime evidence. A shared structured memory consolidates verified facts, artifacts, replay steps, and failed routes across branches, allowing agents to build on collective progress and carry validated knowledge into subsequent milestones. In controlled benchmark environments, DoGNAVY-Exploit with GLM-5.2 achieves 97.5% Pass@1 on Cybench, and 97.5% zero-day and 100% one-day Pass@1 on CVE-Bench. On ExploitGym, it solves 79 tasks with GLM-5.2 and 157 with GLM-5.3, while the corresponding public Claude Code baselines solve 39 and 130 tasks, respectively. Ablation results further demonstrate that the stage-aware orchestration, expert knowledge, parallel exploration, and memory designs can substantially improve the exploitation capabilities of open-weight agents.
papers.title: DoGNAVY-Exploit: Harnessing Parallel Open-Weight Agents for Stage-Aware Vulnerability Exploitation

papers.abstract: Online 3D Gaussian mapping enables fast and high-fidelity novel view synthesis, with broad applications in augmented reality, robotics, and autonomous systems. However, many current methods assume static scenes or filter out dynamics as outliers. In this paper, we study in-view scene changes where objects are manipulated in front of the camera within a single online sequence, unlike prior works that detect changes outside the camera view or between separate captures. This setting entangles transient and persistent dynamics, as objects can be distractors while moving and persistent once they settle. While recent studies start to address distractors by removing them for clean static background, in-view scene changes remain underexplored. To resolve this, we present SettleSplat, a monocular mapping system that maintains up-to-date 3D Gaussian maps under such changes. Specifically, we lift coarse per-pixel uncertainty into Gaussian dynamicity field, then prune transient ones. For persistent changes, we derive geometric contradictions weighted by parameter-free rendered depth uncertainty to separate true changes from under-optimized regions. On Bonn and Co-Fusion, SettleSplat achieves consistent 3D Gaussian maps, outperforming current baselines on both full images and change regions while maintaining comparable speed.
papers.title: SettleSplat: Monocular Gaussian Mapping under In-View Scene Changes

papers.abstract: We present a two-dimensional axisymmetric physics-informed neural network (PINN) of the discharge channel of the P5 Hall thruster at 300 V and 5.4 A, which solves eleven coupled plasma fields and assimilates 145 internal probe measurements per field reconstructed from the data of Haas and Gallimore. The electric potential is obtained from Poisson's equation in charge-separation form, n_e = n_i(1+eta), with eta bounded by construction, which keeps the stiff electrostatic constraint active and trainable. The reference solution agrees with the training profiles to relative L2 errors of 0.017, 0.073 and 0.205 for the potential, electron temperature and ion density, and held-out tests show the potential to be far more robust than the ion density to the withdrawal of measurement lines. We then test the solution against requirements the data fit does not reveal: global particle and current balances, the electron current implied by the momentum equation, the field-aligned electron force balance and the axial ion momentum budget. These expose a neutral inflow six times the measured flow, a bound in the potential representation, and a momentum-implied electron current, more than 99% field-aligned, exceeding the discharge current by orders of magnitude. Correcting these, with a divergence-free magnetic field fitted to measured data, uncertainty-weighted data, the electron pressure gradient and progressively imposed field-aligned and current constraints, yields a solution that conserves particles to within 3%, holds the current between 5.1 and 5.4 A and places 97% of the potential and 88% of the temperature measurements within their uncertainties. Within the tested single-velocity fluid formulation, however, the ion density, potential and ion velocity could not be matched together, and the field-aligned electron balance remains the main obstacle to electron self-consistency.
papers.title: A Two-Dimensional Physics-Informed Neural Network Model of a Hall Effect Thruster Plasma: Self-Consistent Electrostatics and Physical-Consistency Diagnostics

papers.abstract: Medicinal plants are usually identified using practitioners' experience, but reproducible, image based methods can complement this knowledge. We present MEDIPI (MEDIcinal Plant Identification), a statistical machine learning approach that classifies medicinal plant leaves from photographs. From each leaf image we extract 52 interpretable features covering shape, texture, color, and a new scagnostics category. We then classify leaves using a three level hierarchy: shape, then edge type, then species. We also release MedLEA, an open R package with 1,099 leaf images of 31 Sri Lankan medicinal plant species. On this dataset, a hierarchical Random Forest achieved the best overall accuracy (100%) in our comparison of hierarchical and non-hierarchical approaches and eight algorithms: Random Forest, XGBoost, Gradient Boosting, linear discriminant analysis, k-nearest neighbor, support vector machine, probabilistic neural network, and artificial neural network. Adding texture, color, and scagnostic features to shape features raised shape level accuracy from 90% to 97%. Linear discriminant analysis plots show how the trained model separates leaf shapes. Accuracy dropped sharply (23-50%) when training and test data came from different datasets, so generalization across datasets remains a challenge.
papers.title: Statistical Machine Learning for Medicinal Plant Leaves Classification

papers.abstract: Deployed language models are updated continually, and regulators increasingly accept changes that were declared in advance. Showing that an update changed behavior only where it was declared to is a different statistical problem from bounding how much it changed: a useful update is meant to change some decisions, so global disagreement and regression bounds cannot certify it. We formalize the problem with declared change envelopes. Before training, the developer commits to a region of inputs, and every decision that changes outside it counts as leakage. Leakage compares two models, so it can be certified from unlabeled traffic with anytime-valid tests whose sample cost we bound from above and below, and per-update certificates compose into a bound on lifetime drift outside all declared scopes. We measure leakage for LoRA and full fine-tuning, preference optimization, reinforcement learning, and knowledge editing on models from 1.5B to 72B parameters. Narrow updates leak widely: domain and policy LoRA updates keep only about 7-36% of the decisions they change inside the declared scope. Across 256 trained variants, leakage tracks the update's KL divergence to the incumbent on out-of-scope inputs (Spearman 0.94).
